rows.why_long: Underdog higher 2.5 needs 56% per pick for your entry; fair view 79% (fanduel 3.5, moved to this line). Averaging 3.2 over the last 6 games, higher than 2.5 in 88% of them (raw 61%, shrunk 76%). Projects 3.1 (raw 58%, shrunk 75%).
why_points: The pick: Receptions higher 2.5 on Underdog. Each pick has to win 56% of the time for a typical entry to make money; the sportsbooks' fair view (fanduel 3.5, moved to this line) is 79%.
Other apps: PrizePicks 4. This is the best number for the higher side.
Game log, most recent first: 3, 5, 3, 3, 1, 3. Weighted average 3.2; went higher than 2.5 in 5 of 6 games (88% recency-weighted).
Trending up: last 3 games average 3.7 vs 2.3 in the games before.
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±1.1, so the line is 0.6 of those swings below his average (standard deviations) — a modest gap.
PFF unit matchup, for context (in the 2023-25 test it added nothing to the projection, so it is not in the numbers): +7% on his average.
PFF: DAL plays man on 28% of coverage snaps (his opponents so far 25%); he gains 0.88 yds/route vs man and 1.02 vs zone → -0% from scheme.
PFF: DAL allows 1.85 yds/route to WRs after adjusting for the offenses it faced (league 1.57) → +15% against his usual opponents.

PFF: He runs 65% of his routes from the slot (0.83 yds/route there, 0.97 outside); DAL allows 1.83 yds/route to slot WRs and 1.71 outside (league 1.47 / 1.63, opponent-adjusted) → +16% vs his usual opponents.
Projection: we expect 3.1 catches on average; in a typical game 2.8 (a few big games pull the average up, so the typical game is what we compare with the line) — 0.3 above the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 61% and the matchup 58%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 76%, matchup 75%.
Bottom line: we give it 75% to win and it needs 56%. The edge is the difference: +19.3 points; that works out to about +34¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
Risks: low line - one play can decide it.
rows.glance_head: The over looks good: we expect about 2.8 in a typical game vs the 2.5 line, and his recent games and the matchup agree.

rows.why_long: Underdog lower 2.5 needs 56% per pick for your entry; fair view 21% (fanduel 3.5, moved to this line). Averaging 3.2 over the last 6 games, lower than 2.5 in 12% of them (raw 39%, shrunk 24%). Projects 3.1 (raw 42%, shrunk 25%).
why_points: The pick: Receptions lower 2.5 on Underdog. Each pick has to win 56% of the time for a typical entry to make money; the sportsbooks' fair view (fanduel 3.5, moved to this line) is 21%.
Other apps: PrizePicks 4. Another app has a better number for the lower side; take that one.
Game log, most recent first: 3, 5, 3, 3, 1, 3. Weighted average 3.2; went lower than 2.5 in 1 of 6 games (12% recency-weighted).
Trending up: last 3 games average 3.7 vs 2.3 in the games before.
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±1.1, so the line is 0.6 of those swings below his average (standard deviations) — a modest gap.
PFF unit matchup, for context (in the 2023-25 test it added nothing to the projection, so it is not in the numbers): +7% on his average.
PFF: DAL plays man on 28% of coverage snaps (his opponents so far 25%); he gains 0.88 yds/route vs man and 1.02 vs zone → -0% from scheme.
PFF: DAL allows 1.85 yds/route to WRs after adjusting for the offenses it faced (league 1.57) → +15% against his usual opponents.

PFF: He runs 65% of his routes from the slot (0.83 yds/route there, 0.97 outside); DAL allows 1.83 yds/route to slot WRs and 1.71 outside (league 1.47 / 1.63, opponent-adjusted) → +16% vs his usual opponents.
Projection: we expect 3.1 catches on average; in a typical game 2.8 (a few big games pull the average up, so the typical game is what we compare with the line) — 0.3 above the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 39% and the matchup 42%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 24%, matchup 25%.
Bottom line: we give it 25% to win and it needs 56%. The edge is the difference: -31.3 points; that works out to about -56¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
Risks: low line - one play can decide it.
rows.glance_head: Pass: we expect about 2.8 in a typical game vs the 2.5 line — if anything the other side.
